# EDS 223 HW 2 - Redlining and Environmental Injustice


## Part 1
Create a map of historical redlining neighborhoods, including:
neighborhoods colored by HOLC grade
an appropriate base map

Load packages and data
```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(tidyverse)
library(spData)
library(knitr)
set_theme(theme_bw())
```


```{r}

ej_screen <- st_read('data/ejscreen/EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb')

redline <- st_read('data/mapping-inequality/mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json')

crashes <- st_read('data/SWITRS_LA/Crashes.csv')
```


LA county
```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# # filter to a state you are interested in
# california <- ej_screen %>%
#   dplyr::filter(ST_ABBREV == "CA") 

# # find the average values for all variables within counties
# ca_counties <- aggregate(california,
#                               by = list(california$CNTY_NAME),
#                               FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)


# filter to a county you are interested in
la <- ej_screen %>%
  dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME %in% c("Los Angeles County"))
```

crashes needs cleaning! make lat and long numeric

```{r}
crashes_clean <- crashes |> 
    mutate(POINT_X = as.numeric(POINT_X),
           POINT_Y = as.numeric(POINT_Y)) |> 
    filter(!is.na(POINT_X), !is.na(POINT_Y))
```


make the csv into a spatial object so we can assign the crs
```{r}
crashes_sf <- st_as_sf(crashes_clean,
                  coords = c("POINT_X", "POINT_Y"),  # x first, then y
                  crs = 4326)                 # WGS84

st_crs(crashes_sf)  # now check it
```

check other crs

```{r}
st_crs(la)
st_crs(redline)
```


```{r}
# make la fit with the other crs
redline <- st_transform(redline, 3857)
crashes_sf <- st_transform(crashes_sf, 3857)
```

try mapping

```{r}
tm_basemap(server = "Esri.WorldTopoMap") +
tm_shape(la, bbox = redline) + 
    tm_polygons(lwd = 0.3) +
tm_shape(redline) +
    tm_polygons(fill = 'grade', lwd = 0.1,
    fill.legend = tm_legend("HOLC Grade")) +
tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom")) +
tm_title("HOLC Grade by Neighborhood in Los Angeles County") +
tm_legend(position = tm_pos_out("left", "center")) +
tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in(
      "right",
       "bottom"))
       
```

### Create a table summarizing the percentage of census block groups that fall within each HOLC grade

```{r}

# Join using within
holc_bg <- st_join(la, redline, join = st_within ) 

# group by the grading and then add a column with the percentage in each grade
 holc_bg |>
  group_by(grade) |>          
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  mutate(percent = n/sum(n)) |> 
  kable()
```

### Create at least two visualizations summarizing current conditions (from the EJScreen data) within HOLC grades using the mean of the following variables (you may combine variables in a single visualization or look at a single variable per plot):
% low income
percentile for Particulate Matter 2.5
percentile for low life expectancy
Use ggplot for your visualizations! You will first need to calculate mean of each variable grouped by HOLC grade.

```{r}
# group by means
holc_means <- holc_bg |>
  group_by(grade) |>
  summarise(low_income_pct = mean(LOWINCPCT, na.rm = TRUE),
            pm25_ppm = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
            low_life_exp_pct = mean(LIFEEXPPCT, na.rm = TRUE))

```

plot by variable

```{r}
# pivot longer
holc_long <- holc_means |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(low_income_pct, pm25_ppm, low_life_exp_pct), 
               names_to = "Injustices",   
               values_to = "Mean_disparity")  

# plot and use facet wrap to show all 4
ggplot(holc_long, aes(x = grade, y = Mean_disparity, fill = grade)) +
   geom_col() + 
   facet_wrap(~ Injustices, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = "Average disparity levels by HOLC Grade",
        x = "HOLC Grade",
        y = "Average level",
        fill = "Grade")

```

#### Interpretation
In the graph above we can see that for both percentage of low income households and percentage of low life expectancy that as HOLC grade gerts worse (closer to 'D' rating), the average level of each variable increases. Neighborhoods with higher pedestrian fatalities are also experiencing more environmental and health challenges. This pattern suggest a potential relationship that could be explained by historical redlining practices. People residing in low-income neighborhoods may not be receiving the same government attention and funding for proper infrastructure as their high-income counterparts.


## Part 2
Your second task is to explore the legacy of historical redlining in Los Angeles on the report of pedestrian and bike crashes/ fatalities.

Description
For this assignment, you must produce the following based on observations from 2020-2025:

## A figure summarizing the percent of observations within redlined neighborhoods within each HOLC grade

Create a visualizations that shows:

- The percentage of bike and pedestrian crashes and fatalities within each HOLC grade
- Include an appropiate title, axis labels, and legend
*Hints*: Make sure to filter for bike and pedestrian crahes(PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT and BICYCLE_ACCIDENT). Look at the difference in NAs between POINT_X/POINT_Y and LONGITUDE/LATITUDE before you decide which to use. Ensure the SWITRS data and HOLC dataset have matching CRS’, then perform a spatial join to assign each crash to a corresponding HOLC grade.


```{r}

bikeped <- crashes_sf |>
  st_filter(la) |>                   
  st_join(redline, join = st_within)     

bikeped_summary <- bikeped |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(ACCIDENT_YEAR >= 2020 & ACCIDENT_YEAR <=2025) |> 
  filter(BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y" | PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y") |>
  drop_na(grade) |>  
  group_by(grade) |>
  summarise(crashes = n()) |>
  mutate(percent = (crashes)/sum(crashes))                      # percents for both

```


```{r}
ggplot(bikeped_summary, aes(x = grade, y = percent, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_col() +
    labs(title = "Percentage of bike and pedestrian crashes (and fatalities) between 2020-2025", 
        x = "HOLC Grade", 
        y = "Percent",
        fill = "Grade")

```
